name: Gao Nang Thom Cho Dao
summary: A long-grain rice from Mỹ Lệ, in the old Cần Đước land. One crop a year, 170 to 185 days, sown in lunar June or July and cut in lunar December. The provincial tourism center says the cooked rice is fragrant and glossy, and also says the variety has lost that flavor. Both stay. A price is Check on arrival.
origin: Xã Mỹ Lệ, xứ Chợ Đào, which the article still calls Cần Đước, Long An. The homepage names the rice among the old Long An goods. Not the Holy See's lunch.
texture: The grain is long. Broken open, the inside is the pink of a pomegranate seed. Cooked, the center says the grains look glossy, as if tossed with oil, and still smell fragrant the next day.
taste: Fragrant as soon as the pot boils, then fragrant, sticky, and good to eat. The same article says the rice no longer has that character, because the variety degenerated after a closed dike ended the yearly flood, salt, and silt, and because chemical fertilizer has tired the soil.
A ward official on that article says the commune is restoring the variety, has marked 200 ha, and is still finishing a geographical indication. No certificate number was printed.
howToEat: Cook it as rice, or carry it as a gift. The article says people still ask for it at Tết.
A price is Check on arrival.
where: Mỹ Lệ and Chợ Đào. The article does not name a shop. Check on arrival.
seoDescription: One-crop rice from Mỹ Lệ, 170 to 185 days, fragrant when it boils. The same article says the variety has lost that flavor. A price is Check on arrival.
